Hi all,

Thanks for the clear list, Sara. I've pulled together technical answers and an exported access matrix (redacted_access_matrix.csv) — see summary below and attached CSV. Mina has included proposed DPA redlines in a Docx and will follow up on legal points.

Technical summary (answers to their bullets):
1) PII classification: Redwood classifies identifiers into three buckets: Personal Identifier (direct identifiers: name, SSN, MRN), Pseudonymous Identifiers (tokenized IDs, hashed IDs), and Non-PII (aggregated telemetry). We will map Acme's questionnaire fields to these buckets; sample mappings included in CSV.

2) Data flows & caching: Our serving runtime may keep ephemeral KV cache and prefix cache in GPU-local memory and a short-lived in-memory cache on the node. Persistent storage (for model checkpoints) is in our storage subsystem which is encrypted at rest. Default runtime retention for KV/prefix caches is session-scoped (max 24 hours) unless customer-configured longer retention; we set default request logs retention to 30 days for hosted customers; dedicated/private can be changed per contract.

3) Subprocessors & locations: Current subprocessors that may process EU personal data include: CloudInfraCo (VMs, Frankfurt region), ObjectStoreProvider (object storage, NL), and LogAnalyticsInc (aggregated telemetry processing, Ireland). Full subprocessor list and country mapping attached as part of legal redlines doc.

4) KMS proof & audit logs: We can provide a redacted audit export for a sample key rotation and an example of an envelope lookup. Attached is a sanitized sample audit export (redacted lines in the CSV) and a pointer to our KMS integration doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeOnboard.

Action items completed: attached redacted_access_matrix.csv; I exported the most recent role bindings with PII flags redacted.

Attachments: redacted_access_matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Please let me know if you want the dataflow diagram in Visio, PNG, or a scanned PDF; we can provide a sanitized PNG for procurement review.

-Neha
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sara,

Attached are the draft redlines to the DPA (redlines_DPA_acme.docx) and the current subprocessor disclosure. Key legal points:

- We can accept most of Acme's standard EU data processing terms with two exceptions we flagged in the redlines: (i) narrower deletion SLA for ephemeral caches in host mode; (ii) stronger limitation on logging retention for GPDR-covered fields unless customer configures otherwise.

- Subprocessor disclosure: We list primary subprocessors and regions in the redlines doc. If Acme requires customer-specific data residency guarantees, we can offer Dedicated or Private deployment options with contractual commitments.

- Cross-border transfers: By default, for hosted customers, we rely on standard SCCs and our EU-based processing stack where possible. For strictly-onshore EU-only processing, recommend Dedicated contract with region pinning.

Next steps: if Acme is comfortable with the redlines, please confirm and we will issue a DocuSign envelope for the DPA and an operation SOW describing retention and auditing artifacts. I included a proposed small concession on cache-deletion SLA to help close.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
